paper.title: Detecting an Odd Restless Markov Arm with a Trembling Hand

settings.name_in_paper: Odd arm identification with restless Markov arms and a trembling hand
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Arms are restless Markov processes (environment markovian), out of scope from ontology v0.5.
unmapped: Each arm is an ergodic finite-state Markov chain; odd arm has transition matrix P1, others P2; P1 and P2 known to the learner
Fixed-confidence odd-arm identification (delta-correct stopping rule for all odd arm locations)
Trembling hand: intended arm pulled w.p. 1-eta, uniformly random arm w.p. eta > 0; the actually pulled arm is observed
settings.definition_quote: We consider a multi-armed bandit with $K\geq 3$ arms ... The Markovian evolution of states on one of the arms (known as the \emph{odd} arm) is governed by a transition probability matrix $P_1$, and the evolution of states on each of the non-odd arms is governed by $P_2$ ... the decision maker however has a trembling hand ... The unobserved arms continue to undergo state evolution, making the arms \emph{restless}.

symbols.R_star: R^*(P_1,P_2): sup over stationary randomised policies of min over alternative odd arm h' of the ergodic state-action occupancy-weighted KL divergences of delayed transition laws

source.label: prop:lower_bound
source.quote: Let $\eta\in(0,1]$ and $h\in\mathcal{A}$ be fixed. Assume that $\mathcal{H}_h$ is the true hypothesis. ... Then, \liminf_{\epsilon\downarrow 0}\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\epsilon)}\frac{E_h[\tau(\pi)]}{\log(1/\epsilon)}\geq \frac{1}{R^*(P_1,P_2)}

results.notes: Paper's epsilon (error probability) mapped to delta. Algorithm class: policies with error probability <= epsilon for all odd arm locations (Pi(epsilon)). Bound on expected stopping time.

source.label: lem:pi_star(L)_in_Pi(epsilon)
source.quote: Fix error probability $\epsilon>0$. If $L=1/\epsilon$, then for every $\delta>0$, $\pi^\star(L,\delta)\in\Pi(\epsilon)$.

results.notes: Delta-correctness of the stopping rule; proof shows error probability <= 1/L. Paper's epsilon is delta here.

symbols.delta_pol: the policy parameter delta > 0 (approximation slack for the near-optimal SRS policy)

source.label: prop:upper_bound
source.quote: Fix $h\in\mathcal{A}$ and $\delta>0$, and let $\mathcal{H}_h$ be the true hypothesis. The policy $\pi^\star(L, \delta)$ satisfies \limsup_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_h[\tau(\pi^\star(L, \delta))]}{\log L}\leq \frac{1+\delta}{R^*(P_1,P_2)}.

results.notes: Stated in terms of log L; with L=1/epsilon this is log(1/delta) in canonical notation. Paper's delta is a policy parameter, renamed delta_pol.

conditions: arms time-homogeneous ergodic Markov on finite state space

source.label: prop:main_result
source.quote: Consider a multi-armed bandit with $K\geq 3$ arms in which each arm is a time homogeneous and ergodic Markov process ... Fix $\eta\in (0,1]$ ... the expected time required by the decision maker to identify the odd arm satisfies \lim_{\epsilon\downarrow 0}\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\epsilon)}\frac{E_h[\tau(\pi)]}{\log(1/\epsilon)}=\lim_{\delta \downarrow 0}\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_h[\tau(\pi^\star(L,\delta))]}{\log L}= \frac{1}{R^*(P_1,P_2)}.

results.notes: Theorem establishes an exact asymptotic characterisation (matching lower bound is Proposition 1, recorded in r1). Recorded here as the asymptotic upper bound achieved by the family pi*(L,delta) in the double limit.
